questions.q: What is the full form of CLR in the .NET Framework?
questions.e: CLR is the Common Language Runtime, the execution engine of .NET that provides memory management, security and exception handling.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the .NET Framework.
I. MSIL is specific to the CPU on which the program was compiled.
II. The JIT compiler of the CLR converts MSIL into native machine code at run time.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. MSIL (Microsoft Intermediate Language) is CPU-independent, and the JIT compiler converts it to native code for the current machine.

questions.q: In .NET, the ______ converts MSIL code into native machine code at run time.
questions.e: The Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler of the CLR translates MSIL into native code for the current machine when a method is first called.

questions.q: What is the full form of GAC in .NET?
questions.e: The Global Assembly Cache is a machine-wide store for assemblies that are shared by several applications.

questions.q: In .NET, the automatic release of memory held by objects that are no longer referenced is done by the ______.
questions.e: The CLR's garbage collector reclaims unused objects from the managed heap, so programmers need not free memory explicitly.

questions.q: Which file is the XML-based configuration file of an ASP.NET application?
questions.e: Web.config stores settings such as connection strings, authentication and session options. Global.asax holds application event handlers.

questions.q: The handlers for application-level and session-level events such as `Application_Start` are written in which ASP.NET file?
questions.e: Global.asax (the ASP.NET application file) contains event handlers such as Application_Start, Session_Start and Application_Error.

questions.q: Which ADO.NET class is used to open a connection to a Microsoft SQL Server database?
questions.e: SqlConnection establishes the connection. SqlCommand runs statements, SqlDataReader reads rows and DataSet holds disconnected data.

questions.q: Which ASP.NET validation control makes sure that a user does not leave a text box empty?
questions.e: RequiredFieldValidator checks that the associated control has a value. The others check ranges, comparisons or custom rules.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a file extension used in ASP.NET web applications?
questions.e: .jsp belongs to JavaServer Pages. .aspx is a Web Forms page, .asmx a web service and .ascx a user control.

questions.q: Which part of the .NET Framework defines the minimum set of rules that a language must follow so that its code can interoperate with code written in other .NET languages?
questions.e: The Common Language Specification (CLS) is the set of rules for cross-language interoperability. The CTS defines the common data types.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ASP.NET page life cycle.
I. The Load event occurs before the Init event.
II. The Unload event occurs before the PreRender event.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. The order is Init, Load, PreRender, Render and finally Unload.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a client-side state-management technique in ASP.NET?
questions.e: Session state is stored on the server. Cookies, query strings and view state keep their data on the client side.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about C# types.
I. Boxing converts a value type such as `int` into the reference type `object`.
II. Unboxing extracts the value type back from an `object`.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. Boxing wraps a value in an object on the heap, and unboxing retrieves the value from that object.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ADO.NET.
I. A DataAdapter acts as a bridge between a DataSet and the data source.
II. A DataSet needs an open database connection all the time that it is being used.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The DataAdapter fills the DataSet and updates the source. The DataSet is disconnected and works in memory, so statement II is false.

questions.q: In C#, a delegate is best described as a ______.
questions.e: A delegate is a type-safe object that refers to one or more methods. Events in C# are built on delegates.

questions.q: Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF), Windows Communication Foundation (WCF) and Windows Workflow Foundation (WF) were introduced with which version of the .NET Framework?
questions.e: .NET Framework 3.0 added WPF, WCF, WF and CardSpace on top of the 2.0 CLR. Version 3.5 later added LINQ.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about VB.NET.
I. The `Shared` keyword is the equivalent of the C# keyword `static` for class members.
II. The VB.NET `Static` keyword declares a member that belongs to the class rather than to an instance.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only I is correct. In VB.NET, Shared makes a member belong to the class. Static is used for local variables that keep their value between calls.

questions.q: What is the default session timeout in ASP.NET, if it is not changed in Web.config?
questions.e: The sessionState timeout attribute defaults to 20 minutes of inactivity, after which the session is abandoned.

questions.q: By default, ASP.NET stores the view state of a Web Forms page in a hidden field named ______.
questions.e: The page's control state is serialised into the hidden field __VIEWSTATE and posted back with the form. __EVENTTARGET names the control that caused a postback.
